name: LLM & Generative-AI Security
description: Security and privacy of large language models and generative AI: prompt injection, jailbreaks, and LLM-assisted security.
narrative:
The earliest work in this area at USENIX Security treated large models mostly as leaky training artifacts rather than as interactive systems to be attacked. "Extracting Training Data from Large Language Models" (2021) showed that verbatim memorized secrets could be pulled back out of a deployed model, and the same threat model was soon carried over to image generators in "Extracting Training Data from Diffusion Models" (2023). Around the same time, generative-AI security broadened beyond pure extraction to ownership and misuse harms, with "Glaze: Protecting Artists from Style Mimicry by Text-to-Image Models" (2023) defending creators against text-to-image mimicry and "DiffSmooth" (2023) using diffusion models themselves as a robustness tool.

The arrival of instruction-following chatbots in 2024 shifted the field decisively toward adversarial prompting and abuse of the model as an agent. Jailbreaking became a first-class topic with "Making Them Ask and Answer: Jailbreaking Large Language Models in Few Queries via Disguise and Reconstruction" (2024) and the automated, scalable "LLM-Fuzzer: Scaling Assessment of Large Language Model Jailbreaks" (2024). At the same time, researchers began documenting real-world misuse and supply-chain risks: "Malla: Demystifying Real-world Large Language Model Integrated Malicious Services" (2024) cataloged underground LLM services, "Instruction Backdoor Attacks Against Customized LLMs" (2024) poisoned custom GPTs, and "What Was Your Prompt? A Remote Keylogging Attack on AI Assistants" (2024) revealed side channels in deployed assistants. A parallel and fast-growing thread used LLMs offensively for security work, from "PentestGPT" (2024) to LLM-assisted fuzzing of embedded and IoT systems in "Fuzzing BusyBox" (2024) and "From One Thousand Pages of Specification to Unveiling Hidden Bugs" (2024).

By 2025 the area had matured into a back-and-forth between attack, defense, and the security of LLM-based agents and pipelines. Defenses became more principled, exemplified by "JBShield: Defending Large Language Models from Jailbreak Attacks through Activated Concept Analysis and Manipulation" (2025), while attacks moved up the stack into retrieval and agent infrastructure with "Topic-FlipRAG" (2025) and "Make Agent Defeat Agent: Automatic Detection of Taint-Style Vulnerabilities in LLM-based Agents" (2025). Privacy concerns re-emerged in new forms, including "Membership Inference Attacks Against Vision-Language Models" (2025) and the human-factors finding that "Malicious LLM-Based Conversational AI Makes Users Reveal Personal Information" (2025).

Today the area spans a wide front: memorization and membership-inference privacy, jailbreak attack-and-defense, agent and RAG security, human-subjects studies of trust and disclosure, and the dual-use of LLMs to both find and repair vulnerabilities, as in "Logs In, Patches Out" (2025) and "PATCHAGENT" (2025). The trajectory is clear, from worrying about what models leak, to what users can trick them into saying, to how to secure entire LLM-driven systems and the agents built on top of them.

milestones.title: Extracting Training Data from Large Language Models
milestones.note: foundational work showing deployed LLMs memorize and leak private training data

milestones.title: Extracting Training Data from Diffusion Models
milestones.note: extended the memorization-extraction threat from text models to image diffusion models

milestones.title: Glaze: Protecting Artists from Style Mimicry by Text-to-Image Models
milestones.note: broadened generative-AI security to creator ownership and misuse, defending against style mimicry

milestones.title: Making Them Ask and Answer: Jailbreaking Large Language Models in Few Queries via Disguise and Reconstruction
milestones.note: established jailbreaking of chat LLMs as a core attack class with an efficient method

milestones.title: PentestGPT: Evaluating and Harnessing Large Language Models for Automated Penetration Testing
milestones.note: launched the offensive LLM-assisted security thread by automating penetration testing

milestones.title: Malla: Demystifying Real-world Large Language Model Integrated Malicious Services
milestones.note: first systematic look at real-world underground LLM-powered malicious services

milestones.title: JBShield: Defending Large Language Models from Jailbreak Attacks through Activated Concept Analysis and Manipulation
milestones.note: marked the shift to principled, internals-based jailbreak defenses

milestones.title: Make Agent Defeat Agent: Automatic Detection of Taint-Style Vulnerabilities in LLM-based Agents
milestones.note: signaled the move toward securing LLM-based agents as full software systems
